summary: Resolves a colour token to its LAST occurrence in the file, so a document writing two themes as two tables has one theme silently unmeasured and the other measured.
impact: With day and night as two tables, `contrast` measured night only; `tokens-used` then reported the design system's own day table as 18 offenders 'valeur_differe_de_celle_du_design_system' - the file disagreeing with itself.
workaround: One row per token with Day and Night as separate columns. `contrast` reads the first column, so Day is now machine-verified and Night is not.
residual_risk: The Night column is not machine-checked. Its ratios were computed with the same WCAG formula and are recorded in the document, and the gap is disclosed there rather than left implied.

summary: A token declared `on:` a background it is never actually drawn on is measured there and reported as a real contrast offender.
impact: `--color-text-inverse` was listed `on: --color-surface-raised`, producing an 'offender' of 1.17:1 describing a text-on-surface combination the app never renders.
workaround: The `on:` list now contains only the accent and semantic fills. An `on:` entry that is not true is not neutral - it manufactures a false failure that looks real.

summary: There is no `unregister` command, so a deliverable registered by mistake cannot be removed through the tool.
detected: 2026-10-02, while registering the first screen file
detail: Screens belong in state.screens via `register <anchor> screen <key> <path>`. I first used `register ... deliverable ...`, which created a second registry entry pointing at the same file. Both now track the same hash and all guards pass, so the duplicate is cosmetic -- but it means every edit to that file must re-register TWICE or `content_hashes_current` and `no_content_drift` fail.
fix: Register screens with kind=screen. If a deliverable entry was created by mistake, re-register it after every edit rather than trying to delete it.
tool_defect: `state.js hash <root> <key>` with an extra `deliverable` segment silently prints state instead of hashing; the documented fix for a drifted screen hash is `register`, not `hash`.

summary: Reported states:0 for every component and still passed, because the state tables' name column was not backticked and the heading was the English 'States' rather than the template's French 'États'.
impact: The gate appeared to verify that a component's states are propagated to every screen that renders it, and verified NOTHING. A design system with zero state declarations and a green component-parity is the worst case: the control looks like proof and is not. This is the same class of failure as forge-guard passing a PRD with 7 critical contradictions.
why_it_matters: component-parity is the only gate that asks whether a component gained a state and every screen renders it. Silently reading zero states removes the app's defence against a component having two renderings.
fix: Template compliance, not a workaround: screen.md.tmpl and design-system.md.tmpl both specify '**États**', and the parser needs a separator (':', em dash or en dash) on the SAME line plus backticked name cells. Now 40 states across 8 components are read and enforced.
residual_risk: skipped_headings still lists 27 headings, so a section that is malformed enough to be skipped is skipped silently. Verified manually that all 8 component sections now parse.

summary: Reads the design system's FIRST value column, so a two-column Day/Night token table has only its day theme machine-checked.
impact: Night-theme contrast ratios are claimed by the document but re-derived by no tool.
fix: Disclosed in design-system.md section 1.1 with the full set of night ratios stated, and the gap named as a weaker guarantee than the day column's rather than left implied.
residual_risk: accepted: a change to a night value would not be caught by contrast. Mitigated by the day/night pairing being written in one row, so the two are edited together.

summary: The brief told the settings/onboarding agent to file source-unavailable under module:more, which contradicted its /browse route.
detail: I assigned it module 'more' because the Mihon verdict table lists it in More's neighbourhood. But it is reached FROM Browse and its back stack must stay on Browse's shell, so it is a browse state, not configuration. The agent flagged the contradiction rather than silently picking one -- which is the correct behaviour and the reason it was caught.
fix: module -> browse in both the frontmatter and section 1. The route was always right; only the module label was wrong.
lesson: A brief that assigns a module and a route can hand an agent two answers. When they conflict, say which is authoritative rather than assigning both.

summary: Declared foreign keys in the drift schema and assumed they would be enforced. They were not: SQLite disables foreign-key enforcement per connection by default.
detected: 2026-10-02, by running the schema rather than reading it
detail: app_database.dart declared CASCADE on chapters.novelId and RESTRICT on history_entries.novelId. Two tests failed against a schema that looked entirely correct. SQLite ships with `PRAGMA foreign_keys` OFF per connection and it is not part of the file format, so a database created with it on reopens with it off unless every connection sets it.
impact: SILENT, not loud. Without the pragma the RESTRICT never fires, so deleting a novel would silently delete the reader's history -- which is exactly B32's forbidden failure. B32 would have read correctly in the schema, in the review and in the documentation, and would not have held. This is SKILL.md 4.5's failure mode (a constraint that is only re-read) in a harder form: here the constraint was not merely unreviewed, it was unenforceable while appearing correct.
fix: `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` in a setup hook on the real connection, plus a test asserting PRAGMA foreign_keys == 1 so a future refactor fails a test instead of disabling B32. The in-memory test instance applies it too -- without that, the tests that catch this bug would themselves not have FK enforcement.
residual_risk: WAL and other connection modes must set it per connection. NativeDatabase.createInBackground owns that one connection; any future second connection must repeat the pragma.

summary: The command documented in AGENTS.md does not run as written; it prints usage.
detail: `dart run drift_dev schema dump lib/core/database` exits with a usage message. The installed drift_dev's CLI differs from the documented invocation.
impact: The schema snapshot required after a table change could not be produced, so 06-database.md's snapshot step is currently unperformed.
residual_risk: OPEN: the correct invocation has not been established. Must be resolved before the first migration, not before the first table -- the schema is version 1 and has no predecessor, so no snapshot is needed yet.

detail: The command prints 'W These options have been removed and were ignored: --delete-conflicting-outputs' and continues successfully.
impact: AGENTS.md documents that flag. It does nothing, and a silent no-op flag in a documented command is how someone ends up with a stale generated file and blames something else.
fix: AGENTS.md should drop the flag. Not yet changed -- recorded here so the DoD's documented command is corrected rather than left to mislead.

summary: Generated code does not compile at schema version 1: `static const versions = const []` is an untyped List<dynamic>, passed to a parameter typed Iterable<int>.
detail: The emitted file is `class GeneratedHelper implements SchemaInstantiationHelper { GeneratedDatabase databaseForVersion(...) { switch (version) { default: throw MissingSchemaException(version, versions); } } static const versions = const []; }`. Two analyzer errors and one lint follow. The file's own `// ignore_for_file: type=lint` covers lints only, so the `argument_type_not_assignable` ERROR survives it.
impact: `schema generate` is unusable at version 1. It only becomes useful once a second schema version exists.
fix: Not used at v1. lib/core/database/generated/ removed rather than committed: an unused generated file that fails `flutter analyze` violates the Definition of Done, and the alternative -- editing generated code or adding an ignore -- is exactly the two things AGENTS.md forbids.
residual_risk: Re-run it when schemaVersion reaches 2, and expect the same defect until drift fixes it. If it still fails to compile then, record it against the pinned version rather than patching the output.

summary: AGENTS.md documented one positional argument; the command requires two.
detail: Correct form is `dart run drift_dev schema dump <input-file> <output-file>`. With one argument it prints usage and exits 0, so it looks like it ran.
fix: lib/core/database/schema.json written and verified: 6 tables, 38 columns, history_entries.novel_id carrying `REFERENCES novels (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT` and chapter_id `ON DELETE CASCADE`. AGENTS.md corrected.
